Official Transcript of Proceedings

         NUCLEAR REGULATORY COMMISSION



Title:             Mandatory Hearing for Long Mott Energy
                   Construction Permit Application for the
                   Long Mott Generating Station



Docket Number:     (n/a)



Location:          Port Lavaca, Texas



Date:              Tuesday, September 22, 2026




Work Order No.:    NRC-0730                          Pages 1-94


                   NEAL R. GROSS AND CO., INC.
                  Court Reporters and Transcribers
                       1716 14th Street, N.W.
                      Washington, D.C. 20009

                   UNITED STATES OF AMERICA

                 NUCLEAR REGULATORY COMMISSION

                              + + + + +

      MANDATORY HEARING FOR LONG MOTT ENERGY, LLC'S

  CONSTRUCTION PERMIT APPLICATION FOR THE LONG MOTT

                       GENERATING STATION

                              + + + + +

                               TUESDAY,

                       SEPTEMBER 22, 2026

                              + + + + +

                 The    meeting       convened        at   the      Bauer

Community Center, 2300 Hwy. 35 Bypass N, Port Lavaca,

Texas, at 5:30 p.m. CDT, Brett Klukan, Facilitator,

presiding.



PRESENT:

           BRETT KLUKAN, Facilitator

           JEREMY BOWEN, Director, Office of Advanced

                 Reactors (OAR)

           MEHDI REISI FARD, Director, Division of

                 Advanced Reactor Engineering, OAR

           ADRIAN MUÑIZ, Safety Project Manager, OAR

           JOE O'HARA, Environmental Project Manager, OAR




                           NEAL R. GROSS
                    COURT REPORTERS AND TRANSCRIBERS
                      1716 14th STREET, N.W., SUITE 200
(202) 234-4433          WASHINGTON, D.C. 20009-4309        www.nealrgross.com

                         P-R-O-C-E-E-D-I-N-G-S

                                                                    5:30 p.m.

                   MR. KLUKAN:          All right, welcome everyone.

 My     name      is    Brett    Klukan.         It's    my     pleasure       to

facilitate this evening's mandatory hearing on the

Long Mott Energy LLC's construction permit application

for the Long Mott Generating Station.                         We're going to

do our best to make this hearing both engaging and

informative            for   all    attendees,         and     as    to     that

endeavor, we hope that you'll partner with us in

establishing a constructive dialogue.

                   The main purpose of this mandatory hearing

is to receive your feedback and answer any questions

you may have regarding the NRC's review of LME's

construction permit application.                     We will also spend

some       time    as     part     of    our     opening       presentation

describing the NRC's new mandatory hearing process as

documented in the Commission's recently issued policy

statement on mandatory hearings for reactor licensing,

published in the Federal Register on June 8th.                               The

Federal Register citation for the policy statement is

91 FR 34661.             Again, that's 91 FR 34661 for your

interest.

                   Now, just for some general and fundamental

ground rules, I ask that you adhere to civil decorum.


                                NEAL R. GROSS
                        COURT REPORTERS AND TRANSCRIBERS
                          1716 14th STREET, N.W., SUITE 200
(202) 234-4433              WASHINGTON, D.C. 20009-4309          www.nealrgross.com
                                                                                  3

 By that I mean, out of respect for each other, please

don't disrupt the speaking time of others, just as you

wouldn't         want    to   be    interrupted         during     your      own

opportunity to speak.

                   However, let me make this next statement

very clear.         Threatening statements or gestures under

no circumstances will be tolerated and will be cause

for immediate ejection from the meeting.                      If you feel

that you've been threatened in any way, please let me

know, or please let one of the local law enforcement

officers stationed around the room know so that we can

address the situation promptly.

                   Keep in mind that we are transcribing the

meeting to make sure that we fully capture your

comments.         So, you can help us get a clean recording

by identifying yourself, spelling your name when it is

your opportunity to speak, as well as providing any

group affiliation that you would like captured as part

of the record.

                   You can also help us get a clean recording

by minimizing any background noise during the public

comment portion of the meeting or the hearing.                          And as

to that, please take a moment now to silence or turn

off any electronic devices on your persons.                          I'd also

ask, as a courtesy to other attendees, given this room


                               NEAL R. GROSS
                        COURT REPORTERS AND TRANSCRIBERS
                          1716 14th STREET, N.W., SUITE 200
(202) 234-4433              WASHINGTON, D.C. 20009-4309          www.nealrgross.com
                                                                                 4

tends to echo, that if you need to have a side

conversation, please take it to the foyer outside of

the meeting room.

                    We should have plenty of time after our

presentation for those who wish to speak, whether it

be     to        offer    any     questions        or    to    comment,       an

opportunity to do so, up to three hours.

                    If you'd like to speak this evening during

the public comment portion and you have not already

done so, please add your name to the sign-up sheet.

Though, given the number of people that just saw and

think they might want to ask a question, we might just

do it by raising hands.                   I'll go through the sheet

based on those who've already registered and then just

go around the room and see if anyone wants to raise

their hand to ask a follow-up question.                         Okay?

                    So, with that said, you can also provide

comments for the record in writing by email until

October 6th, and we'll provide more information on

that in a later slide.

                    Please note that the exits are directly

behind you, and the bathrooms are just off to either

side of those exit doors.                 And now without any further

ado -- oh, next slide, please.

                    So, this is what I was supposed to be


                                NEAL R. GROSS
                         COURT REPORTERS AND TRANSCRIBERS
                           1716 14th STREET, N.W., SUITE 200
(202) 234-4433               WASHINGTON, D.C. 20009-4309        www.nealrgross.com
                                                                               5

talking from.        But anyway, these are all the rules I

just covered in my opening speech.                  I apologize.          But

next slide.

                  Now without -- now that we're back on

track, now without any further ado, I'll present it --

turn it over to Jeremy Bowen, the Director of the NRC

Office of Advanced Reactors.                  Thank you very much.

Take it away, Jeremy.

                  MR. BOWEN:        All right.             Thanks, Brett.

And good evening and welcome, everyone.                       We're happy

to be here.          We're happy to see all of you.                         We

appreciate you taking the time to come out to this

meeting tonight.          I will tell you all that Texas did

not disappoint.        It was nice and warm when we got here

last night, and so we appreciate the warm welcome.

                  So, as Brett mentioned, we're here tonight

for the -- for the mandatory hearing for the reactor

application that we currently have before us.                       And the

purpose of a mandatory hearing is really outlined in

the Atomic Energy Act.             And the Atomic Energy Act is

the law that governs how the nation's commercial

nuclear reactors and commercial nuclear products are

handled.         So, the Atomic Energy Act basically, when

the nuclear -- excuse me -- the nuclear technology was

being deployed and developed in the '50s and '60s,


                            NEAL R. GROSS
                     COURT REPORTERS AND TRANSCRIBERS
                       1716 14th STREET, N.W., SUITE 200
(202) 234-4433           WASHINGTON, D.C. 20009-4309          www.nealrgross.com
                                                                                       6

there was an interest in making sure that the public

was aware and there was transparency that the -- then

the      Atomic          Energy        Commission,         now     the     Nuclear

Regulatory Commission, was considering an application

whether or not to move forward with a construction

permit for a nuclear plant.

                        So    the     mandatory       hearing      process        has

actually undergone several changes since the Atomic

Energy Act was passed in the 1950s.                            The most recent

change           was    this      past     spring,      and    our    Commission

basically determined at that time that we needed to

provide a little bit more transparency in the process

and      an       opportunity            for     this     public      engagement

interaction, which is why we're here tonight.

                        So that's the purpose of the mandatory

hearing.               We're going to go through and basically

present some information to you about what the NRC is,

what we do, how we conduct our statutory requirements,

how we conduct our safety and environmental reviews,

and give you all an opportunity to ask us questions

about       that        process,         ask   us    questions       about       this

specific project that we have before us.                             We will take

your questions and your feedback, and that will inform

our final decision about whether or not to move

forward with issuance of the construction permit.


                                    NEAL R. GROSS
                             COURT REPORTERS AND TRANSCRIBERS
                               1716 14th STREET, N.W., SUITE 200
(202) 234-4433                   WASHINGTON, D.C. 20009-4309          www.nealrgross.com
                                                                          7

                 This is different than an opportunity to

request a -- what we call a contested hearing, or if

you have a specific concern with the plant.                         That

process was done back in the summer of last year.                      We

did have some requests for that.              Those are proceeding

on a separate path.        This is just a separate mandatory

hearing.

                 So as Brett mentioned, we'll take your

questions and comments, and then there's also an

opportunity to provide some written comments through,

I believe it's October 6th.

                 So, again, we look forward to interacting

with you all tonight.         Appreciate you all coming.             And

with that, I'm going to turn it over to my colleagues

here.       The first will be Dr. Mehdi Reisi Fard, who is

the executive in charge of this project, and he is one

of the directors of the Division of Advanced Reactor

Engineering in the office that we work for.

                 DR. REISI FARD:       Thank you, Jeremy.         Hello

and welcome everyone.          Again, my name is Mehdi Reisi

Fard and as the division director, I'm the senior

leader who oversaw and directed the project team

reviewing this application.             Today's meeting supports

the NRC's mission to protect public health and safety

through the efficient and reliable licensing oversight


                          NEAL R. GROSS
                   COURT REPORTERS AND TRANSCRIBERS
                     1716 14th STREET, N.W., SUITE 200
(202) 234-4433         WASHINGTON, D.C. 20009-4309       www.nealrgross.com
                                                                                   8

and regulation of nuclear technologies, enabling the

safe and secure use of nuclear power.

                    The construction permit is one step in the

process for the deployment of new nuclear technology,

technologies such as the Xe-100 reactor design.                                 In

preparation for the construction permit review, we

held a public meeting here in February of 2024 to

inform the community about LME's plans to request a

construction          permit     for    the    Long      Mott     Generating

Station based on the Xe-100 reactor design.

                    And we discussed the NRC's safety and

environmental           review      process,        as       well      as     the

opportunities for public participation during the

review.          The NRC started the detailed technical review

of LME's application in May 2025, and has recently

completed the environmental review and is working

toward completing the safety review.

                    The remaining activities are to issue the

NRC      safety      evaluation        and    finalize        a     licensing

decision.          If the construction permit is approved, LME

will have NRC approval to build the reactor, Long Mott

Generating Station.                Under our two-step licensing

process, LME must request and receive additional NRC

approval before operating.

                    Today we'll provide more details on our


                              NEAL R. GROSS
                       COURT REPORTERS AND TRANSCRIBERS
                         1716 14th STREET, N.W., SUITE 200
(202) 234-4433             WASHINGTON, D.C. 20009-4309            www.nealrgross.com
                                                                                     9

review process and answer your questions.                                 We look

forward to engaging with you during this meeting.

Next slide, please.

                    This slide provides you with an outline of

the       agenda         for    today.          Following           the      NRC's

presentation, we will conduct a hearing and field your

questions and comments.                   Following today, you will

have the opportunity to send us written comments to

this email address on the screen until October 6th.

After October 6th, the NRC will issue a meeting

summary          about    today's      meeting      and    email        comments

received.          Next slide, please.

                    The NRC regulations are contained in Title

10 of the Code of Federal Regulations, or 10 CFR,

which governs licensing and construction of nuclear

power plants, research and test reactors, uranium

recovery facilities, fuel cycle facilities, waste

depositories,             and    for     medical,         industrial,           and

academic purposes.               Next slide, please.

                    This slide shows the principal legislation

and regulations driving timely decisions and outcomes

for     the      environmental         and    safety      reviews.             More

detailed and comprehensive information about this

legislation          and       our   regulations        can    be     found       by

accessing the link shown at the bottom of this slide


                                 NEAL R. GROSS
                         COURT REPORTERS AND TRANSCRIBERS
                           1716 14th STREET, N.W., SUITE 200
(202) 234-4433               WASHINGTON, D.C. 20009-4309            www.nealrgross.com
                                                                              10

or on the NRC's public website.                    Next slide, please.

                    LME applied for a construction permit for

four units at the Long Mott Generating Station site,

which is covered under 10 CFR Part 50 and is a two-

step licensing process.                  The first step of the NRC

review is to determine whether it is safe to construct

and operate the nuclear power plant at the site based

on    the        information     submitted        in   the    construction

permit application.

                    In parallel to the safety review, the NRC

also       evaluates       environmental           impacts      from       the

construction and subsequent operation of the nuclear

power plant at the proposed site.                      If approved, LME

may use their construction permits to move forward

with construction of the plant.                        In order for the

plant to begin operation, LME will need to submit an

operating license application to the NRC for review

and approval.

                    I'd    now     like      to     introduce        today's

presenters.           Adrian Muñiz is NRC's Safety Lead for

this        project,      and      Joe      O'Hara       is    the      NRC's

Environmental Lead.              I'll turn things over to them to

give their presentation.                 Next slide, please.

                    MR. MUÑIZ:       So, again, my name is Adrian

Muñiz.           So let's show you at least where we are, or


                               NEAL R. GROSS
                       COURT REPORTERS AND TRANSCRIBERS
                         1716 14th STREET, N.W., SUITE 200
(202) 234-4433             WASHINGTON, D.C. 20009-4309         www.nealrgross.com
                                                                                11

try to show you the licensing process that we're going

to in a little bit more detail.                       So, basically, to

support our licensing decision on whether to grant the

construction permit, we have engaged in safety reviews

and environmental reviews of the application submitted

by Long Mott Energy.

                      For the safety review, the review is still

ongoing and will be documented in a safety evaluation

report that will be made available to the public.                            For

the environmental review, we have completed, actually,

that       review       and     have      issued      an      environmental

assessment and a finding of no significant impacts for

the Long Mott Generating Station.                          We provide more

details in subsequent slides about this.                         Next slide,

please.

                      So, the Long Mott Generating Station is

proposed         to    be    sited     in    Calhoun       County,      Texas,

specifically           adjacent      to     the    Seadrift      Operations

facility owned by the Union Carbide Corporation, which

is an affiliate of Dow Chemical Company.                        The site is

approximately 10 miles from Port Lavaca and 8 miles

from Seadrift.              Next slide, please.

                      This is an aerial view of the location of

the proposed facility.                    As you can see here, the

construction           permit     application         is      proposing      the


                               NEAL R. GROSS
                        COURT REPORTERS AND TRANSCRIBERS
                          1716 14th STREET, N.W., SUITE 200
(202) 234-4433              WASHINGTON, D.C. 20009-4309          www.nealrgross.com
                                                                                12

Exclusion Area Boundary to be set at 400 meters,

that's roughly a quarter of a mile, from the reactor

building.         That's the building that would house these

reactors         that    we    were      alluding     to      before.        The

Exclusion         Area    Boundary        is   the    same      as   the     Low

Population        Zone      and    the    Emergency        Planning       Zone.

That's what is being proposed for this facility.                            Next

slide, please.

                   The reactor technology proposed for the

Long Mott Generating Station, as noted before, is an

X-energy Xe-100 reactor design.                    This is a pebble bed

high temperature gas-cooled reactor.                       It is comprised

of four Xe-100 reactors that will be able to generate

a total of 800 megawatts of heat, which is converted

to about 320 megawatts of electricity from these four

modules that have been proposed to be deployed.

                   In this specific design, fuel pebbles are

continuously rotated through the core, and cooling is

provided by helium, the gas that's used for this

reactor cooling, instead of using water, which is

what's been used or is used for the fleet of nuclear

power reactors that are currently operating in the

United States.             The facility's main purpose is for

generating process steam, is what is being proposed by

Dow Chemical Company for the usage of this reactor


                               NEAL R. GROSS
                        COURT REPORTERS AND TRANSCRIBERS
                          1716 14th STREET, N.W., SUITE 200
(202) 234-4433              WASHINGTON, D.C. 20009-4309          www.nealrgross.com
                                                                               13

technology.             Next slide, please.

                       The fundamental safety functions are the

most important functions performed by different parts

of the plant to protect the workers and the public,

and as such are key aspects of our safety review.                           For

this particular reactor, reactivity and control --

reactivity and power control are achieved through fuel

in the form of pebbles and reactivity control systems,

which includes control rods that are used to shut down

the reactor.

                       The    heat    removal      safety      function       is

achieved through the reactor coolant system and other

passive          and    active       systems     available      for    backup

cooling.          And the radionuclide retention is fulfilled

by the fuel cells with different layers, as shown in

the picture, it will be to your left panel, as well as

other barriers in the facility itself.                         Next slide,

please.

                       So, these are key topics that we evaluate

as part of our review of an application for this type

of facility.                 For example, we take a look at the

effects of external hazards such as nearby facilities,

hydrology, seismology of the area, and the design

features         that        the   design    affords      to   protect      the

facility from such hazards.


                                   NEAL R. GROSS
                         COURT REPORTERS AND TRANSCRIBERS
                           1716 14th STREET, N.W., SUITE 200
(202) 234-4433               WASHINGTON, D.C. 20009-4309        www.nealrgross.com
                                                                                  14

                   Other key aspects of the review of course

is     the       reactor    fuel      itself      and        the     means       of

controlling and safely shutting down the reactor in

order to protect from radiation hazards for both

workers and the public.                Next slide, please.

                   All right.          As alluded before, we are

conducting a review of the CP application, this is

some of the chronology.              It was accepted for review in

May of last year.                The safety evaluation, we are

working right now, we're here today, and as stipulated

before, to receive comments from you and questions

that we will take into consideration as we continue

our review of this application.

                   In terms of the primary day for completing

our decision of this, we are targeting by the end of

November for the issuance of the safety evaluation.

We will take your questions again on today and those

received until October 6th as we continue our review.

                   In addition, and not shown on this slide,

but I wanted to make you aware that we did receive a

revision to the application this Friday, this past

Friday.           We   have     made     --    the    portions          of     the

application that are publicly available, we've made

them available to the public in ADAMS, accession

number ML26261A419.            And we are also in the process of

                         1716 14th STREET, N.W., SUITE 200

                                                                               15

putting direct links on our public website for you to

be able to access that application.                          And with that,

I'm going to turn it over to Joe.

                   MR. O'HARA:          Thank you, Adrian.                 Good

evening, everyone.             For those of you I didn't get a

chance to meet during the open house, I'm Joe O'Hara.

 I'm the environmental project manager assigned to the

Long Mott Generating Station.                      You know, as Mehdi

mentioned, the proposed action here is to decide

whether or not to issue a construction permit to Long

Mott Energy that would allow the construction of the

Long Mott Generating Station.

                   And as we alluded to,                it's a two-part

process.          If in the future an operating license

application is submitted to the NRC, then the NRC

would        perform     additional         environmental           reviews,

reviews          based     upon       any      new      or      significant

environmental changes that have taken place since

construction.            So a construction permit does not

authorize operation.

                   For the environmental review, we had a

team of 28 environmental experts that analyzed the

results of the environmental report submitted by Long

Mott Energy as part of their application.                       The NRC and

Long Mott Energy's environmental team began biweekly


                              NEAL R. GROSS
                       COURT REPORTERS AND TRANSCRIBERS
                         1716 14th STREET, N.W., SUITE 200
(202) 234-4433             WASHINGTON, D.C. 20009-4309          www.nealrgross.com
                                                                              16

discussions about the information the NRC would need

in addition to what was submitted in the application,

and there were 84 additional information needs related

to the project over the majority of the environmental

resource areas that were analyzed.

                   Our team conducted a site audit with Long

Mott Energy in September of 2025, and we were able to

resolve approximately 60 percent of all of those

information needs that we needed at that two-day

meeting.         And I believe it was September 8th and 9th.

 The remaining aspects we'll resolve over the course

of the next two months.

                   In December of 2025, the NRC conducted an

environmental site visit along with members of the

U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and the National Marine

Fisheries Service at Seadrift.                    We toured 10 areas of

the site related to the environmental resource areas

including aquatic and terrestrial ecology, water,

threatened and endangered species, and land use.                           And

these efforts we used to gather information for use in

consultations with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service

and the National Marine Fisheries Service.

                   In    May     of    2026,      the    NRC   issued      the

environmental           assessment         with      a   finding      of     no

significant impact across all of the resource areas

that we analyzed.         Next slide, please.             Okay.    So, the

NRCS staff concluded that a finding of no significant

impact was achievable for all the resource areas

identified.         You     cannot      issue      an     environmental

assessment without a finding of no significant impact.

 The finding of no significant impact is contained

within the EA along with the exemptions that we will

require to issue the EA.

                 There'll be a QR code on the next slide

where if you have a smartphone that's capable of

detecting the code, you can do it right from your seat

and the actual environmental assessment will download

to your phone.        Okay.     Next slide, please.

                 And there you go, folks, if you have a

smartphone, you can pull it out and record this QR

code and it will be downloaded directly to your phone.

 If you prefer not to do that, there's an ADAMS

accession number there, and the -- ADAMS number is

Management System.           If you enter that ADAMS number

ML26112A016 from any Google-capable computer, you can

download it to your home computer.                        Okay.    So I'm

                 MR. KLUKAN:         All right, thank you very

much.       So, just to recap, the purpose of the mandatory

hearing, which is again what we're conducting this

evening, is threefold.                 Two of these we've already

addressed this evening.               The first, to explain how the

                   And we've also discussed or described

the handout that we've offered in the back is a list

of    all        the    links     we've     provided       through      today's

presentation, and again, those handouts or everything

in the back is for you to take home with you this

evening.              Now, to turn to our next portion of the

mandatory hearing, the Commission's policy statement

provides that the applicant, in this case LME, be

offered an opportunity to provide a presentation of no

more than 30 minutes about the project and the license

application.

                       Consistent with that, LME has chosen to

give a statement as part of this hearing.                         Speaking on

behalf           of    LME    will    be    Kreshka      Young,      the      Vice

President of Long Mott Energy and North American

Energy Business Director for Dow.                      And with that, I'll

                       MS. YOUNG:          All Right.           Good evening,

everyone.              As Brett mentioned, my name is Kreshka

Young.           I'm not sure if I need to spell that for the

record, but I will just in case.                      K-R-E-S-H-K-A, Y-O-

U-N-G.           I am the Vice President of Long Mott Energy as

well as the North American Energy Business Director

for Dow.              I also have the privilege as part of that


                                 NEAL R. GROSS
                          COURT REPORTERS AND TRANSCRIBERS
                            1716 14th STREET, N.W., SUITE 200
(202) 234-4433                WASHINGTON, D.C. 20009-4309          www.nealrgross.com

role to lead our internal project team for what we

call Project Long Mott.                  Thank you for the opportunity

to address everyone here this evening.                           We appreciate

the interest from the community.                        We also appreciate

the work of the NRC staff.

                      I want to spend a few minutes talking

about why this project matters to us and to our

workforce.            Dow's Union Carbide Seadrift Operations

site has operated here for over 70 years.

                      Generations of families in this community

have built their lives around this site as employees,

as contractors, and as neighbors.                         And now Long Mott

Energy, which is a wholly owned subsidiary of Dow just
